Would you pay $1
to switch?

Two envelopes. One holds ten times the other. You open one—and the seemingly rational choice leads somewhere strange.

The resolution, as a quiz

Can rare outcomes still dominate the average?

At level n, the pair occurs with chance 2−n−1, but contains 10ⁿ + 10ⁿ⁺¹ dollars. Multiply them to see how much that single level adds to the expected value.

As n rises, does each level’s contribution to the average…

Choose an answer, then inspect the table.

nChance of pairExpected-value contribution

The average does not settle to a finite number.

When expectations are infinite or undefined, familiar rules such as “a guaranteed $1 cost makes you worse off” stop being safe comparison tools.
